re_line: Trump's arms offer to Xi, then a denial · Senators press on Taiwan arms · Fuel exports after Golden Week
editors_note:
Good morning. This is the first China Room Brief: the week behind and the week ahead in US-China relations, plus what CSIS scholars have coming.

A week after Xi Jinping's state visit, Washington is still working out what the summit produced.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Beijing's fuel-export pause meets Golden Week's end
week_at_a_glance.body: China's holiday ends Oct 7, and Lianhe Zaobao reports it is unclear whether Beijing resumes fuel-export approvals after it.
week_at_a_glance.why: Reuters expects the suspension to tighten diesel and jet fuel across Asia.
bullets: Refiners suspended October exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau.
PetroChina cancelled gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes on Sep 30.
The New York Times ties the curbs to dwindling domestic inventories.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Greer's overcapacity move is due "within weeks"
week_at_a_glance.body: USTR Jamieson Greer told Nikkei the US will unveil countermeasures against overproduction from China, Japan and others "within weeks."
week_at_a_glance.why: The summit's tariff relief still has no start date. Greer said no timeline is set for cuts under the Board of Trade mechanism.
bullets: Reuters: the US has slowed aircraft-part exports to China to build leverage.
Greer's "Milwaukee framework" on steel excess capacity, agreed by the 28-member global steel forum, leaves China out (AFP).

week_at_a_glance.headline: IMF and World Bank meet in Bangkok Oct 12
week_at_a_glance.body: The Annual Meetings run Oct 12 to 18.
week_at_a_glance.why: China's growth numbers arrive with fresh support behind them.
bullets: A nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy took effect Oct 1.
The PBOC's 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo is set for Oct 8.
September manufacturing PMIs hit 50.1, ending two months of contraction.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senators press Trump on $14B Taiwan package
heard_on_the_hill.body: Twenty-one Democrats led by Jeanne Shaheen urged Trump to "immediately deliver congressionally approved defense assistance to Taiwan."
bullets: They cite $1.3 billion in appropriated funds and a $14 billion package approved nine months ago.
Four Republican senators separately called for its release.
Armed Services Chair Roger Wicker said US commitments to Taiwan must be upheld after meeting Taipei's representative, Alexander Yui.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson: Taiwan arms aren't trade leverage
heard_on_the_hill.body: Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed suggestions the delayed package is a bargaining chip in trade talks.
bullets: He said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across two terms.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Chinese car ban slips past the midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate put off a bill permanently barring Chinese-made cars until after Nov 3, AP reported.
bullets: Reuters: senators plan a vote in November.
Sen. Bernie Moreno says his separate bill, aimed at automakers more than 15% Chinese-owned, won't touch Mercedes-Benz.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bipartisan bill targets Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senators from both parties proposed barring Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period.
heard_on_the_hill.why: Markets noticed. Shenzhen's ChiNext index fell 4.53% the next trading day.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Starbucks pressed to close Xinjiang stores
heard_on_the_hill.body: A US congressman demanded Starbucks shut its first stores in Xinjiang, citing forced labor, Reuters reported.
